column15: Range spans blended and single pot still (base, IPA Cask, Rum Cask, Pot Still); type left empty. Own site shows no peat mention; Irish whiskey conventionally unpeated outside named exceptions (Connemara, Pearse, Dunville's).
Classic unpeated Speyside malt; sherry- and bourbon-seasoned oak maturation, no peat mentioned anywhere in sourced material.
Lowland style is conventionally the least peated in Scotland; the Wikipedia article only documents historical (1887) peat-fired kilning, not a current spec, so confidence is low.
Classic unpeated Speyside malt, bourbon and French oak casks; no peat mentioned.

Hunter Laing's "Old & Rare Platinum Selection" single-cask range; each release names its source distillery. Distillery rows added for the samples: Arran, Dufftown, Glenturret, Bunnahabhain, Glen Garioch, Highland Park. Parent company "Hunter Laing" itself is not emitted as its own row here; another batch may.

Reference file lists the site as "Lochranza". Arran also bottles a heavily-peated Machrie Moor line alongside its unpeated core range; not disambiguated here since this row only supports resolving "Old & Rare Arran" — left unknown rather than guess which style a bottling is.
Standard unpeated Speyside malt, mostly used for blending and for Singleton of Dufftown.
Standard unpeated Highland malt.

Wikipedia: "one of the milder single malt Islay whiskies"; the Islay article groups it with Bowmore/Bruichladdich/Caol Ila as "substantially lighter in taste" than Laphroaig/Ardbeg. Core range unpeated; its Mòine range is heavily peated (see rule.tsv) per the research brief's own worked example — that specific pairing was not independently re-verified via an opened source.
Historically used peated malt until the mid-1990s, then switched to unpeated; current status not directly confirmed in sourced material, left unknown rather than guess.
Wikipedia: "Highland Park uses the local peat, which contains a higher proportion of heather than many other peats" — moderate, heather-inflected peat, not Islay-heavy.

Known undisclosed/teaspoon brand for Highland Park, named explicitly as a sibling pair in this research task's own brief; peat level assumed identical to parent since it is reportedly the same liquid under another label.
Standard unpeated Speyside malt.
Distinctive meaty/sulphury worm-tub character but unpeated; core Dewar's blending malt.
Hunter Laing's "The First Editions" single-cask range; samples name Speyburn and Craigellachie (both added as distillery rows). Input brand string is singular "First Edition" — aliased below.

German independent bottler and retailer ("Purveyors of Taste"); own site: "We at Maltbarn offer a select choice of whiskies both under our own label and from other bottlers." Samples name Tullibardine, Ben Nevis, Inchgower, Glenburgie, Blair Athol (all added as distillery rows); "Islay Malt" sample too generic to name a specific distillery.
Standard unpeated Highland malt.
Standard range unpeated; owned by Nikka (Asahi Group) since 1989. Occasional peated limited releases exist but are not the house default.
Standard unpeated Speyside malt, key Ballantine's blending component.
Standard unpeated Highland malt, key Bell's blending component.
Standard unpeated Speyside malt, mostly Diageo/Bell's blending stock; also a standalone brand in this batch (Inchgower Flora&Fauna).

Marketed explicitly as a heavily-peated Islay single malt (the "Smokehead" name is built on that identity). Source distillery is officially undisclosed by Ian Macleod; widely rumoured in the trade press to be Bunnahabhain but not confirmed by the producer, so parentSlug is left empty per the brief's rule 3 on undisclosed labels.

Diageo markets "The Singleton" name over three different distilleries depending on region: Glen Ord (Asia), Dufftown (Europe), Glendullan (Americas). parentSlug left empty since no single distillery applies to the bare brand string; region/legalRegion left empty for the same reason. All three source distilleries are unpeated so peat is safe regardless of which resolves. More specific "Singleton of X" rows below carry the real parent when the product name states it.
Diageo's Asia-market Singleton expression, from Glen Ord distillery.
Diageo's Europe-market Singleton expression, from Dufftown distillery.
Standard unpeated Highland malt.

County Down, Northern Ireland (whiskey-GI convention uses IE per the brief). Core range (Single Malt, Double Wood, Small Batch Bourbon Cask, Sherry Finish, Distillers Cut) is unpeated; a separate "Peated" line exists (see rule.tsv). Own site's core range appears to be single malt throughout but this was not fully confirmed, so type left empty.
Standard unpeated Speyside blending malt.
Distinctive "meaty" style (partial triple distillation, worm tubs, "The Beast of Dufftown") but unpeated.

2013 reformulation reduced Islay malt content to Bunnahabhain alone. scotchwhisky.com: master blender wanted to move away from the brand having "lost itself in Islay"; today's blend is described as "lightly to moderately smoky" with floral/oak/fruit/honey/nutmeg notes alongside the smoke.

Blend of "at least 10 malt and grain whiskies from three distilleries (Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Chita)" per Wikipedia; Hakushu is Suntory's smokier/peated-leaning distillery, giving a light smoky element, but Hibiki is not marketed or reviewed as a peated whisky.
Listed as "Blended Scotch Whisky" among Duncan Taylor's own brands. Core range (Black Bull, Kyloe, Kyloe Sherry Finish) unpeated; a separate "Peated" variant exists (see rule.tsv).

Producer/distillery not confidently identified — searches for "King's 107", "King's Rye", "King's Wheated", "King's Ryeconic" returned no usable results. American-whiskey naming (rye, wheated mashbill, proof-designated "107") strongly implies a US whiskey line, so the category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) is applied at low confidence. Range spans rye and wheated bourbon, so type is left empty.

Irish whiskey blend tied to the band's estate. Widely reported in general trade knowledge to be bottled by West Cork Distillers (also in this batch) but that link was not independently confirmed via an opened source, so owner is left empty rather than asserted.
scotchwhisky.com: malt spec is 50ppm, house style "medium-weight and medium-peated"; Wikipedia: "the whiskies are described as of a peat character."

Bardstown, Kentucky bourbon-trail distillery (brands: Blood Oath, David Nicholson, Daviess County, Ezra Brooks, Rebel Bourbon); range spans bourbon and rye so type left empty. American whiskey category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) applied.
Bourbon brand (core, French Oak finish, Cabernet Sauvignon finish variants) produced at Lux Row Distillers.

Believed from general trade knowledge to be a Chinese whisky producer (Goalong Distillery, Hunan), but this was not confirmed via any source actually opened — all searches came back empty. China (CN) has no code in the closed country list, so XX is used rather than guessing a listed code.

No identifiable web presence found under any spelling tried. Input gives only the bare name "Maen" three times with no distinguishing sample product name, so origin, type and owner could not be determined.

Models "Seagram's V.O." Canadian whisky. Wikipedia: "Seagram's V.O. is produced by Sazerac" following the 2000 break-up of the original Seagram company (assets split between Diageo, Pernod Ricard and others). The sample "100 Pipers 1970's (Seagram's)" is a different, Pernod-Ricard-India-owned Scotch blend that merely carries the historical Seagram name in some listings; not modeled by this row.

Independent bottler revived 1993 (original 1826 Glasgow distillery closed 1907); also owns Ardnamurchan distillery, not relevant here since this batch's samples ("Adelphi", "Adelphi Maclean's Nose") name no specific source distillery.

Site footer credits "Mossburn Distillers Ltd, a Marussia Beverages company" — the same owner as Torabhaig. Named after Knock Castle (Caisteal Chamuis / Castle Camus) on the Sleat peninsula, Skye, near Torabhaig; likely a blended malt released while Torabhaig's own stock matured, but exact composition and peat level were not confirmed.
No identifiable web presence found (searches only returned an unrelated TV editor of the same name). Input samples are just the bare name twice, no further evidence.
Standard unpeated Speyside blending malt.

Marketed as "Japanese blended whisky" ("Oni" demon + "Kishi" knight); brand page describes cedar/lightly-smoked malt notes alongside dominant floral and honey character in both expressions (Demon Knight, Deadly Sakura) — not marketed as a peated whisky. Milestone Beverages may be a distributor/marketing brand owner rather than the actual distiller.

Founded 2014 in Rüdenau, Bavaria, Germany. Catalogue lists both "St.Kilian Classic" and "St.Kilian Peated" — could not confirm which is the true baseline or the peated variant's level; producer's own site was unreachable (TLS certificate mismatch on st-kilian-distillers.com) and no other source with the detail was found. Flagged for reviewer; no rule added for the Peated variant given the lack of a citation.

No peat or Islay-content mention found in sourced material. Company's own distilleries (Jura, Fettercairn, Tamnavulin per the Scotland distillery reference file) are predominantly unpeated, but the blend's exact recipe was not directly confirmed, hence low confidence.
Standard Diageo blended Scotch since 1884; no peat or smoke character mentioned in sourced material.
No identifiable web presence found for this exact brand; single-product own label, left fully unresolved.

Brand itself was not independently confirmed via an opened source (no hits found); "Canadian Whisky" category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice; Canadian whisky is conventionally a blend) applied based on the name and sample "Small Batch" wording.

Believed from general trade knowledge to be a budget blended Scotch (commonly associated with MacDuff International); could not independently verify the producer via any source actually opened, so owner is left empty. Category default (unpeated blend) applied.

Irish Distillers' innovation/experimental range, produced at Midleton, spanning single malt, single pot still and single grain (Pernod Ricard's own brand list confirms it in their portfolio). Type left empty (spans several). Peat left unknown rather than assumed "none": an experimental range could plausibly include a peated release and none of the sources opened confirmed either way.

New Midleton Distillery produces Jameson, Powers, Redbreast, Green Spot and others; standard Irish whiskey, conventionally unpeated ("peat is rarely used in the malting process outside of Scotland" per the Irish whiskey article). Range spans pot still/grain/malt so type left empty.
Generic name, no identifiable web presence found; single-product own label.
Brand not independently verified via any source actually opened (no hits found); American-themed name suggests US whiskey, category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) applied.
Brand not independently confirmed beyond the category (no hits found); Canadian whisky category default (conventionally a blend, conventionally unpeated) applied.
Brand not independently verified via any source actually opened; American-themed name, category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) applied.
Peat is rarely used in the malting process outside of Scotland per the Irish whiskey article; producer not independently confirmed beyond the category default.

Suntory's flagship single malt; generally unpeated (Suntory's peated house style sits with Hakushu instead). The Wikipedia article does not mention peat at all, consistent with — though not an explicit statement of — an unpeated core range.
